candidates.draft_body:

'And after this law I made known unto thee the days of the Sabbaths in the desert of Sin which is between Elim and Sinai. And I told thee of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I told thee of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years' — Jubilees frames the book's entire content as the divinely-revealed system of Sabbaths-AND-jubilees given to Moses on Sinai. The book IS Mäṣḥafä-Kufāle ('Book of Divisions') — the canonical book-OF-divisions of time. Tewahedo liturgical-cosmology preserves Jubilees' Sabbath-and-jubilee structure as the canonical framework for the Tewahedo täzkar (commemoration) calendar: every Tewahedo täzkar is calculated using the Jubilees-Mosaic Sabbatical-of-Sabbaticals system, anchored in this verse.

'And the jubilees will pass by, until Israel is cleansed from all guilt of fornication, and uncleanness, and pollution, and sin, and error, and dwelleth with confidence in all the land, and there will be no more a Satan or any evil one, and the land will be clean from that time for evermore' — Jubilees presents an explicit eschatological-cleansing of the land, with Satan removed, and the land permanently clean. The Tewahedo eschatological-hope draws canonical anchor here: the final consummation is not merely individual-spiritual-resurrection but cosmic-territorial-cleansing-and-the-permanent-removal-of-demonic-presence. The Tewahedo distinctive emphasis on the consecration-of-the-land (the Tewahedo's sacred-geography tradition that sees specific Ethiopian holy mountains and lakes as canonically-sanctified-territory) finds canonical anchor in Jubilees' jubilee-of-jubilees-eschatology.

'These are the words and the regulations regarding the sabbaths of the Lord, as they were written down for the children of Israel and the angels of God, that they may keep them, and not violate them throughout all their generations' — closing-sabbath regulations. Tewahedo sabbath theology (the historical Tewahedo observance of BOTH Saturday-Sabbath and Sunday-Lord's-Day, unique among the major Christian communions until the 17th century — and still preserved in some monastic communities) draws on Jubilees 50 as canonical anchor for the centrality of Sabbath observance.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'But the Sabbath day of the Lord thy God ye shall not do any work thereon, but that which ye have prepared for yourselves on the sixth day, so as to eat, and drink, and rest, and keep Sabbath from all work on that day, and to bless the Lord your God, who has given you a day of festival, and a holy day; and a day of the holy kingdom for all Israel is this day among their days for ever' — Jubilees inscribes the Sabbath as 'a day of the holy kingdom for all Israel' — a day liturgically tasting the Kingdom of God in advance. Tewahedo Saturday-Sabbath theology (uniquely among major Christian communions in preserving Saturday-Sabbath alongside Sunday-Lord's-Day) reads the Sabbath as canonical foretaste-of-the-Kingdom. The Tewahedo monastic Saturday-vigil tradition (more elaborate than Sunday in some monastic communities) draws warrant from Jub 50:9's 'holy kingdom day' framing.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'Whoever does any work thereon, or goes a journey, or tills (his) farm whether in his house or any other place, and whoever lights a fire, or rides on any beast, or travels by ship on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or slaughters a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths: the man who does any of these things on the Sabbath shall die' — Jubilees gives the strictest possible Sabbath-prohibition list, with the canonical 'shall die' formula. The Tewahedo Saturday-Sabbath observance preserves this strictness in canonical-pastoral form: Saturday is a day of complete rest, abstention from agricultural-and-commercial work, and elevated-spiritual-focus. The Tewahedo's distinctive observation of BOTH Saturday (canonical-OT Sabbath) and Sunday (Christ's-resurrection-Lord's-Day) gives the Tewahedo the canonical-fullness of weekly-time-sanctification, anchored in Jub 50.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And every man who does any work thereon, or goes on a journey, or tills (his) farm, whether in his house or any other place, and whoever lights a fire, or rides on any beast, or travels by ship on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or slaughters a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths: The man who does any of these things on the Sabbath shall die' — the most severe Sabbath prohibition in Jubilees. The closing book is given Moses on Sinai — the inclusio with 1:1 closes. **Tewahedo canonical reception**: this is the closing word of Mäṣḥafä Kufāle, and the Tewahedo Sabbath tradition takes its severity seriously even as it interprets the death-penalty language as covenantal-spiritual rather than civil.
